title: THE GOD WHO WOUNDS AND HEALS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'There is no god besides me. I put to death and I bring to life, I have wounded and I will heal, and no one can deliver out of my hand. I lift my hand to heaven and solemnly swear: As surely as I live forever, when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand grasps it in judgment, I will take vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me. I will make my arrows drunk with blood, while my sword devours flesh.'" — Deut 32:39b-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God declares His absolute sovereignty in words that are both awesome and comforting: "I put to death and I bring to life, I have wounded and I will heal." There is no power in the universe that rivals His. Life and death, wounding and healing — all are in His hands, and "no one can deliver out of my hand." This is a God of complete authority over everything that exists.

At first this might seem frightening. But for the child of God, it is profoundly reassuring. If God holds all power, then nothing can touch us apart from His permission and purpose. The same hand that wounds is the hand that heals. God is not the author of random cruelty; even the hard things He allows are held within His sovereign, loving purposes, and He is able to bring healing and restoration.

This truth has steadied believers through the darkest valleys. When we suffer, we are not at the mercy of blind chance or hostile powers. We are in the hands of the sovereign God who wounds and heals, kills and makes alive — and who works even our pain toward good for those who love Him (Rom 8:28).

Supremely, this points to Christ. On the cross, God's own Son was wounded for our healing — "by his wounds we are healed" (Isa 53:5). And in the resurrection, the God who brings life from death conquered the grave. The God who holds life and death in His hands has used that power to save us. Rest in His sovereign hand, for no one can pluck you out of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does God's complete sovereignty frighten me or comfort me — and why?
2. How does trusting the God who "wounds and heals" help me in suffering?
3. How does Christ's death and resurrection show God's power used to save?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, all power over life and death is in Your hands, and nothing can pluck me from Your grip. Help me trust that the hand that wounds also heals. Thank You that by Christ's wounds I am healed. Amen.
